name: FaultyTerminal-TS-TW
title: Faulty Terminal
description: A full-screen green terminal grid of tiny glyphs that clump into drifting cloud shapes, with scanlines, flicker and noise, plus a cursor that brightens a ripple near it.
use: You want a cyberpunk or error-state backdrop that suggests a broken screen behind an alert or 404.
avoid: The busy green grid and flicker make body text hard to read, and the effect runs continuously.
a11y: The glitch and flicker run constantly and ignore reduced-motion, which can be uncomfortable; the canvas has no label. (keyboard: n-a, labels: n-a, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: Black filled with a fine grid of tiny pale-green glyphs and squares, clustering into soft clouds and bands so the surface reads like a malfunctioning terminal display. White text sits over the centre, and faint scanlines and curvature suggest a curved CRT screen.
behaves: The green glyph clusters drift and flicker, with sections cutting out and returning as the noise field moves. Moving the cursor adds a bright ripple around the pointer, and a load animation fades the grid in from the edges.
customise: Props set scale, grid multiplier, digit size, time scale, pause, scanlines, glitch, flicker, noise, chromatic aberration, dither, curvature, tint, brightness, mouse reaction and its strength.
weight: heavy: A full-screen WebGL shader with layered noise, glyph, scanline and glitch passes every frame.
demo: A white heading 'System failure' with the line 'A glitching CRT grid that reacts to the cursor.'
issues: Constant flicker and glitch can be uncomfortable and ignore reduced-motion.
The dense green glyphs make the small overlaid tagline hard to read.
The busy grid would overwhelm any body text placed on top of it.
polishWhy: Convincing broken-CRT texture, but the dense flicker is busy and the subtitle is hard to read.
